key_insight: OMOP standardization plus NLP and PSA-based rules substantially improved prostate cancer data capture from EHRs, making the dataset more usable for research.
clinical_relevance: Better-structured prostate cancer records can support more reliable outcomes research, registry validation, and future precision oncology studies.
method: Transformed UTMB Epic EHR data for registry-identified prostate cancer patients into OMOP CDM v5.4.
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical notes.
Applied PSA-based algorithms to identify missing treatments and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: The pipeline produced 815 analytic cases, with 700 (85.9%) complete and concordant with the cancer registry, PSA showing excellent agreement, and NLP markedly improving sparse Gleason/stage capture.
watch_item: Performance depends on data quality, and both structured EHR fields and cancer registry entries can contain gaps or errors, so results may need local validation before deployment.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
